title: Excel Sheet Column Number and Title
statement:
Spreadsheet columns are labelled `A`, `B`, ..., `Z`, then `AA`, `AB`, ..., `AZ`, `BA`, ..., `ZZ`, then `AAA`, and so on. Column `1` is `A`, column `26` is `Z`, column `27` is `AA`, column `52` is `AZ`, and column `703` is `AAA`.

You are given `q` queries, each a single token. If the token consists of digits, it is a column number and you must print the matching column title. If it consists of uppercase letters, it is a column title and you must print the matching column number.

Answer every query, one result per line, in the order given.

**Follow-up:** Each direction is often asked on its own in interviews (title to number, or number to title). Make sure you can derive both and explain why this is not a plain base-26 conversion.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `q`.
Each of the next `q` lines contains one token: either a positive integer (a column number) or a string of uppercase letters (a column title).
outputFormat: Print `q` lines. For a number token print its column title; for a title token print its column number.
constraints: Every column number is between 1 and 10^9
Every title is the title of a column number between 1 and 10^9 (so it has at most 7 letters)

examples.explanation: `A` is column 1. Column 28 is `AB` (26 columns `A`-`Z`, then `AA`, `AB`). `AB` is 1*26 + 2 = 28. Column 701 is 26*26 + 25, so letters 26 (`Z`) and 25 (`Y`): `ZY`.
`ABC` is a title: 1*26^2 + 2*26 + 3 = 731. The other two are numbers: column 52 is `AZ`, and column 703 is `AAA`, the first three-letter title.

complexity.time: O(q · L), where L ≤ 7 is the title length

hints: Title to number is a base-26 conversion where `A`..`Z` stand for 1..26: `value = value * 26 + letter`.
Number to title is the reverse, but there is no zero digit, so the usual `n % 26` breaks at multiples of 26.
Subtract 1 before every division: `n -= 1; letter = n % 26; n //= 26`, and reverse the letters at the end.
